scenes.say: Could your script accidentally take down production? How do you make sure that never happens?

rows.b: Only act if not already correct
Show what would happen, no changes

scenes.say: Here’s how you keep scripts safe: check before changing anything, add a dry-run mode, log every action, and always get your code reviewed.

scenes.title: Error Handling
scenes.say: Use strict error handling in Bash, and run shellcheck to catch bugs before your script hits production.
Never store secrets in your script. Pull them from the environment or a vault instead.

scenes.question: What makes a script safe in prod?
scenes.right: Idempotent checks, dry-run, error handling, logging, code review, secrets from a vault.
scenes.say: If you’re asked what makes a script safe in production, don’t just say you tested it. Mention idempotent checks, dry-run, strict error handling, logging, code review, and secure secrets.
